conviction_note: The findings sum to -0.7 and the scaled number is -1.0 (p_up 46 x abs 12.5). The Q3 quarter probably lands inside its guide: orders covered >70% of the midpoint, and Europe and batteries are strong. The print turns on the Q4 guide and the 2027 framing. Every counterparty and industry series published since the July 28 call points to a softer US residential market than management described (SEIA/WoodMac permits, SolarEdge, Sunrun). Those are public proxies that agree with a +28.7-point put skew and a 7-of-8-down reaction history, so they are probably mostly priced. A 23% short float with 6.35 days to cover argues against pressing them. The two measurements agree in sign and size, and the lean is small.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $305.15M consensus and EPS $0.50 (Seeking Alpha preview, 2026-10-26, https://seekingalpha.com/news/4657185-enphase-q3-2026-earnings-preview). This equals the midpoint of the company's own guide of $290-320M incl ~$75M safe harbor (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001463101/000146310126000080/a2026q2exx991pressrelease.htm). Finviz carries EPS next Q $0.51 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=ENPH), so two estimate sources agree with each other and with the guide. The Q4 bar is NOT directly sourced. It is implied at about $300M from FY2026 consensus revenue of $1.18B (S&P Global via https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/enph/forecast/) less Q1 $282.9M, Q2 $291.9M and Q3 cons $305M. So the Q4/guidance finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Finviz on 2026-10-27 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=ENPH): short float 22.96%, short ratio (days to cover) 6.35, short interest 29.42M shares. That is a crowded short, the same band as the two squeezes recorded in LESSONS. Baseline: 25d skew +28.72 vol points (puts paid), event-implied move 11.48%, ATM IV 144%, put/call OI 1.0. Spot $31.79 is 56% off the 52-week high after a May SST/AI spike to about $68 fully retraced. The 20-day run-up is -0.13%, but the stock fell about 9% on Oct 14 on Morgan Stanley (UW, PT 27->24) and Susquehanna (PT 37->35) cuts and a Deutsche Bank short-term sell catalyst call of Oct 7 (PT $34). The bearish setup is public and well positioned.

findings.finding: SEIA/Wood Mackenzie's Q3 2026 Solar Market Insight (published September 2026, after Enphase's July 28 call) shows US residential Q2 installs at 995 MW: -12% YoY, -10% QoQ, the lowest in five years. California permits fell 25% and Illinois permits 20%, the 2026 forecast was cut to -23% (from -21%), and 2H26 interconnections are expected at 1.6 GW vs 2.1 GW in 1H (-24% half on half). On July 28 management guided global sell-through up ~10% QoQ in Q3 'primarily from the US'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A soft forward guide drove -15.15% after Q3 2025 (2025-10-28) and -14.16% after Q2 2025. A strong Q1 guide drove +38.6% after Q4 2025 (2026-02-03). The guide is the line this name trades on.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (SEIA/WoodMac US Solar Market Insight Q3 2026; primary page https://seia.org/research-resources/solar-market-insight-report-q3-2026/ returned 403)
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public industry series, so it is probably largely priced: the stock fell from ~$37 to ~$32 between August and October and the skew is +28.7. What would be different if it were fully priced: Q4 implied consensus would sit below Q3, not flat at ~$300M (FY $1.18B). The series contradicts management's 'US-led growth' framing, which the call has to reconcile in the Q4 guide.
findings.independence: This is an industry proxy, not an Enphase number. It points the same way as SolarEdge's Aug 5 US commentary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/solaredge-technologies-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-05/) and Sunrun's Aug 5 cut (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001469367/000162828026053349/exhibit991q226.htm). Those are three different documents on one theme (weak US resi), sized separately and small.

findings.finding: SolarEdge (Q2 call, 2026-08-05, a week after Enphase spoke) said US residential softness continues in Q3 with no usual seasonal pickup. It said installers face tax-equity constraints and FEOC uncertainty, and that distributors are reducing purchases and inventory. It also guided Europe ~$15M down sequentially on seasonality. Enphase in July described its own microinverter channel inventory as 'somewhat high' and planned shipments below demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Channel destocking commentary paired with soft guides produced the -14% to -16% reactions of 2025 (Apr, Jul, Oct 2025 prints).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a direct competitor's statement made after Enphase's last guide, but it is 12 weeks old and public. The ENPH stock drift since August suggests it is partly priced. If it were fully priced, Q4 revenue consensus would not be roughly flat to Q3.
findings.independence: This is a direct competitor sharing distributors, a step closer than the SEIA series. It shares the weak-US-resi theme with the SEIA and Sunrun findings, as noted there. Company 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001419612/000117891326003833/exhibit_99-1.htm

findings.finding: Sunrun (8-K, 2026-08-05) reported Q2 subscriber additions of 19,793, -31% YoY. It cut its FY26 Aggregate Subscriber Value guide to $4.6-4.9B from $4.8-5.2B and its Cash Generation guide to $200-375M from $250-450M, citing affiliate-channel volumes weakening. Affiliate installers are a TPO channel where Enphase equipment is used. Sunrun's storage attach rate reached a record 74%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as above: the forward guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and 12 weeks old. Sunrun is mostly a Tesla Powerwall shop, so the read-through to Enphase is indirect. Enphase's own TPO strategy (safe harbor with TPO partners) partly hedges it.
findings.independence: This is a counterparty/peer document, different from SEIA and SolarEdge, but on the same theme. It is a proxy for Enphase.

findings.finding: The Q4 bar is demanding against the safe-harbor mix. FY2026 consensus revenue is $1.18B (S&P Global via stockanalysis). Q1 was $282.9M, Q2 $291.9M and Q3 consensus is $305M, which implies a Q4 consensus of about $300M, flat to Q3 even though Q3 includes ~$75M of safe harbor. Deutsche Bank's Oct 7 short-term sell call (PT $34) estimates 2026 safe-harbor revenue at ~$255M. With Q1 $34.5M, Q2 $84.3M and Q3 guide ~$75M, that leaves ~$61M for Q4, so core revenue must rise from ~$230M to ~$240M into a seasonally weak US Q4. DB says 2027 consensus needs ~33% organic growth and sits 21% above its own 2027 profit forecast. Management disclosed $1.1B of executed safe-harbor agreements, so Q4 safe harbor could stay high, which is the upside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 guide (given 2025-10-28) -15.15%. Q1 2026 guide (given 2026-02-03) +38.6% when it beat a depressed bar. The guide decides the sign on this name.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-14 (DB call dated 2026-10-07 per the article's correction note of 2026-10-16)
findings.why_not_priced: The DB call and the Oct 14 sell-off show the bear case is visible. What is not visible in a single number is that the FY consensus still embeds a roughly flat Q4. If the Street had absorbed DB's 2027 view, FY27 revenue consensus would not be $1.20B (+1.5%) with EPS $2.13. The Q4 bar is derived arithmetic from one estimate source, so the finding is capped small.
findings.independence: FY consensus: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/enph/forecast/. Safe-harbor history: Enphase Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001463101/000146310126000080/a2026q2exx991pressrelease.htm. $1.1B executed SH agreements (the counter-evidence): https://reportify.cn/news/1279983061236453376

findings.finding: Europe is a counterweight to the US. In Q2 Enphase's Europe revenue rose ~35% QoQ, sell-through ~30%, and Netherlands battery activations +102%. Dutch net metering ends 2027-01-01. Zonneplan counted 21,439 new Dutch home-battery registrations in Q2 2026 (+128% QoQ), and DNE Research forecasts an unprecedented 4.5 GWh of Dutch residential storage in 2027. That supports Enphase battery shipments (guided 130-150 MWh in Q3, G5 battery shipping Q4) through the Q4 guide. Net of the rest: Europe must offset a US that SEIA projects -24% half on half. SolarEdge guided Europe seasonally down ~$15M in Q3, which tempers the size.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe strength in Q2 2026 (+35%) was met with -3.44%. The name has not paid for European strength alone.
findings.why_not_priced: The Dutch-language battery data and the 2027 net-metering cliff are not in US sell-side previews, which focus on 25D and US TPO (Zacks/SA). If they were priced, the FY27 consensus debate (DB) would credit European storage. It is a segment item, sized net of the US.
findings.independence: Enphase's own Q2 call (Europe +35%, NL activations +102%): https://reportify.cn/news/1279983061236453376. Zonneplan registrations: https://www.zonneplan.nl/thuisbatterij/aantal-thuisbatterijen-nederland/

findings.finding: Q3 should land inside the guide. On July 28 management said orders already covered over 70% of the Q3 revenue midpoint, and that it was shipping ~$15M below demand to trim channel inventory. Q3 consensus ($305.15M) sits exactly at the guide midpoint. ENPH has beaten non-GAAP EPS consensus the last two quarters (Q1 $0.47 vs $0.37, Q2 $0.46 vs $0.40) and the stock fell both times.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. It lands inside what the company guided and the market was told to expect, so it is sized near 0.
findings.independence: EPS beat history: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ENPH/earnings-forecasts (per search snippet; page 403 on fetch).

findings.finding: The short is crowded into the print: 22.96% of float short, 6.35 days to cover, 29.42M shares (Finviz, 2026-10-27). The stock sits at $31.79, 56% below its 52-week high and back at its pre-May levels, after two sell-side cuts and a DB sell catalyst call in October. A Q4 guide that merely holds roughly flat, or new safe-harbor/SST news, meets a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From a depressed, heavily shorted base, an above-bar guide produced +38.6% on 2026-02-03.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism, not information. The skew (+28.7) pays for downside, so the market is not paying for the squeeze tail. If it were, call IV would be bid relative to puts.
findings.independence: The Oct 14 sell-off on MS/Susquehanna cuts confirms bears pressed into the print: https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62365615/why-is-enphase-energy-stock-falling-wednesday

findings.finding: Enphase front-ran the call with AI-data-center news. On Oct 26 it announced 900 V GaN bidirectional switch devices with Infineon for its IQ solid-state transformer, and on Oct 27, before the print, an SST lab demo of 13.8 kV AC to 800 VDC (Finviz headlines). The May 2026 SST announcement coincided with the stock going from ~$36 to ~$68 in four weeks. Management targets a full-function system by end-2026, customer pilots in 2027 and commercial shipments in 2028, so any pilot customer named on the call is a non-solar catalyst.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The SST news of May 2026 coincided with a doubling of the stock that fully retraced by October. There is no print-day history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock rose ~4% on Oct 27 intraday (30.36 -> 31.63), so part of it is in. Revenue from SST is 2028, so it moves the multiple only if the call adds a customer or a pilot date.
findings.independence: Same company, two releases: the Oct 27 SST milestone headline on https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=ENPH. Weekly price path: Yahoo chart https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ENPH?range=6mo&interval=1wk

findings.finding: Tesla (8-K, 2026-10-21) deployed 13.7 GWh of storage in Q3 2026 vs a company-compiled consensus of 15.9 GWh (-14%), and storage revenue fell ~16% YoY. It is a weak read on residential storage demand, since the figure is mostly Megapack and Powerwall is not broken out.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and a week old, with a weak transmission to Enphase. It is a proxy, sized small.

findings.finding: A further $11.0M of IEEPA tariff refunds was received in July 2026, after the $41.0M in Q2 that added 15.6 points to Q2 GAAP gross margin. It will flatter Q3 GAAP gross margin but is excluded from non-GAAP, and nothing links it to the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $45.4M refund recognition (GAAP GM 60%) was met with -3.44%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was disclosed in July, so it is priced. It is a one-off below the non-GAAP line and is sized at a fraction.

baseline_tension: Most of what I found (US resi weakness from SEIA, SolarEdge, Sunrun and Tesla, plus DB's 2027 skepticism) agrees with the +28.7 put skew and the 7-of-8-down reaction history, so it is likely priced. The cuts against it are a 23% short float with 6.35 days to cover, Europe/battery strength and an AI-SST narrative pushed into the print. That leaves only a slight negative lean (p_up 46, not 40).
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short 23% float / 6.35 DTC; negatives agree with skew) and rule 5 (proxies, not company numbers): SEIA -1.5 -> -1.0, SolarEdge -1.0 -> -0.7, Sunrun -0.7 -> -0.5
Rule 6 (Q4 bar not directly sourced, derived from one FY estimate source): Q4 bar finding -1.0 -> -0.8 and kept small
Rule 1 (beats sold twice in 2026): Q3 order-coverage finding +0.3 -> +0.2. Rule 9 (segment net of the US): Europe +0.8 -> +0.7

p_up 44 -> 46 for the crowded short and the negatives agreeing with the skew. abs_move_pct left at 12.5 (guidance-driven, hunters' sizes historically too small). Positioning, SST, Tesla and tariff findings unchanged
